artifacts.name: low-level-design
artifacts.description: Low-Level Design for NFR-PERF-003: TTI <3s enforcement via Lighthouse CI, Vite code splitting, React.lazy, and bundle size budgets

summary.work_completed: Created LOW_LEVEL_DESIGN.md for NFR-PERF-003 covering Vite manualChunks strategy, React.lazy Viewport deferral, Lighthouse CI configuration, bundle size budgets, error handling, and security considerations
key_findings: Three.js (~600 KB gzipped) must be isolated in its own chunk and deferred behind React.lazy to keep critical path < 200 KB
Lighthouse CI with .lighthouserc.json asserts TTI < 3000 ms on 10 Mbps throttled desktop profile
Vite manualChunks splits three, r3f, bvh, zustand/immer, and idb into separate long-term-cached vendor chunks
Named Three.js imports (not import * as THREE) are required for tree-shaking to work
CSP compatibility verified: dynamic import() is native ESM and does not require unsafe-eval

human_review_required.item: Lighthouse CI GitHub App token setup
human_review_required.reason: LHCI_GITHUB_APP_TOKEN requires a GitHub App installation for PR status checks. Document setup steps before implementation.
If Tailwind generates any inline styles, this conflicts with NFR-SEC-002 CSP. Verify Tailwind JIT produces no inline styles.

recommended_actions: Verify Vite manualChunks strategy is consistent with existing vite.config.ts scaffold
Confirm .lighthouserc.json TTI threshold of 3000 ms is achievable given Three.js bundle size
Check CSP compatibility between NFR-PERF-003 (dynamic import) and NFR-SEC-002 (CSP headers)
Approve or request changes via PR #28 design review
